Stingy

/STIN-jee/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Stingy means unwilling to spend or give money, holding tightly to every cent.

Stingy means unwilling to spend or give money, holding tightly to every cent. Everyone enjoyed dinner with Uncle Ray until the check arrived, because he was famously stingy and would study the bill for ten minutes rather than leave a fair tip.

Worked Example

The office manager was so stingy with supplies that employees had to sign a form to receive a single new pen, and he kept the box of paper clips locked in his own desk drawer.

Rationing pens and locking up paper clips shows an unwillingness to spend or hand out even the tiniest amounts, which is exactly what makes the manager stingy.

How Stingy Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

miserly

miserly: hoarding money and hating to part with it

tightfisted

tightfisted: gripping money tightly, reluctant to spend

cheap

cheap: avoiding spending even when fairness calls for it

Antonyms

generous

generous: giving freely and willingly

openhanded

openhanded: giving readily, without holding back

How Strong Is It? — frugal → miserly → stingy

frugal vs. stingy

frugal vs. stingy: A frugal person spends carefully and hates waste, while a stingy person refuses to spend or give even when fairness calls for it.

miserly vs. stingy

miserly vs. stingy: A stingy person grips their money tightly, but a miserly one hoards it obsessively while living as though they had nothing.

Root — sting

Suffix — -y

Put it together

Put it together: Stingy is a homegrown English word of uncertain origin. One popular theory ties it to a dialect word meaning 'sharp-tempered, stinging,' from Old English stingan, 'to sting,' picturing someone prickly and sharp about money. Because the connection is unproven and no reliable root family exists, there is no root quiz for this word.

Use the root in a new word: sting

Use the root in a new word: sting: Stingy's true origin is unproven, but the favorite theory ties it to sting, from Old English stingan — picturing someone so sharp and prickly about money that parting with a single cent stings.

Strength Check

Word Choice

informal, conversational

Stingy is an everyday, mildly insulting word for someone unwilling to spend or give. It describes habits with money and generosity, not physical sensations; a wasp's sharp jab is a sting, never stingy. In formal writing, miserly or parsimonious strikes a more elevated tone.
